limitations.summary: No production authentication, authorization, RLS or ABAC enforcement is implemented.
Environment-referenced source values exist, but the validated defaults/TOML/env/secret-store configuration model is not implemented.
Deadline expiry does not interrupt detached compiler CPU, in-flight SQLite work or establish common database-native statement cancellation.
DESCRIBE has compiler-only tests but no end-to-end backend or endpoint result evidence.
Snapshot-local source identity exists, but there is no registry, coordinator or multi-source production caller.
Known source-sized ORDER, GROUP, DISTINCT and graph-dedup Rust fallbacks now reject before source I/O; bounded physical implementations remain unavailable.
The parser feature recognizes LATERAL, but both compiler paths reject it and no execution profile is implemented.
The PostgreSQL/MySQL evidence can skip on provider absence and therefore cannot establish production admission.
No sealed W3C RDB2RDF mapping execution matrix exists for MySQL.
The MySQL source-selector branch lacks a positive open_backend selector test.
Production telemetry, health/readiness, graceful shutdown and lifecycle controls remain unimplemented.
Recursive property paths use an exact finite-pair fixed point, but total work/cancellation budgets and live PostgreSQL/MySQL qualification remain open.
The product-mock gold is development-only, maps one table, has a currently red live table/column inventory gate, and proves no image/source provenance or backend admission.
The complete backend contract, live matrix, security, cancellation and conformance gates in ADR-0038 R3 are incomplete.
No pinned SPARQL Protocol manifest is executed; only a tested read-only HTTP subset exists.
One absolute serve-layer deadline exists, but compiler work, rows, bytes, source work, recursion and native cancellation do not form one total QueryBudget.

Narrow private diagnostics include same-byte static RootPie preflight, a counterfactual non-authority bubblewrap name/path inventory, and late seccomp; actual host byte consumption/runtime closure, the minimal production dependency closure, and exact-artifact release proof are not implemented.
Validated immutable snapshot reload and schema-drift readiness handling are not implemented.
Serve compilation consumes startup PK/FK/uniqueness facts without later-DDL exclusion or generation invalidation, so constraint-sensitive plans are not production-admissible.
Post-200 SELECT/CONSTRUCT failures terminate the body and may expose a usable prefix; they cannot become RFC 9457 responses.
Remote-source TLS verification and a production secret-store transport remain unimplemented.

claims.text: DESCRIBE CBD compilation has required compiler-only tests; this does not establish backend or endpoint execution.
Full SPARQL 1.2 Query or Protocol conformance is not claimed.
PostgreSQL and MySQL have live query and endpoint evidence, but those suites can still skip and do not establish production admission.

Sealed required-live PostgreSQL RDB2RDF execution records 57 passes, one documented deviation and five exact skips across 63 R2RML cases, plus 23 passes and one exact skip across 24 Direct Mapping cases; this is mapping evidence only and does not establish production admission.
Sealed SQLite RDB2RDF execution records 62/63 R2RML cases passing with one documented deviation and 19/24 Direct Mapping cases passing with five exact skips; this is mapping evidence only.

Stale-constraint safety, total-resource-qualified recursive paths, bounded global operators, federation, total request governance, security/identity, observability/lifecycle and an exact production artifact remain planned.

The canonical product-mock development KAT seals all 139 gold artifacts and 171 development source files, then qualifies one narrow ProductDesign/Style R2RML vertical against live PostgreSQL; it proves no image/source provenance or production admission.
The separate 11-database/112-table/598-column table-and-column inventory currently fails closed on observed drift and grants no qualification.
None of SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL is production-admitted under ADR-0038 R3.

SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL compilers use exact finite-pair fixed points for recursive P+/P*; hostile required execution is SQLite-only, while live PostgreSQL/MySQL qualification and total resource governance remain open.
Pre-response HTTP failures and startup CLI surfaces are redacted; correlation IDs have no telemetry sink and post-200 stream failures cannot become atomic RFC 9457 responses.

SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL source selectors feed one immutable source/backend/compiler/cache binding; reachability is not admission. PostgreSQL introspection and unqualified base-table resolution are `public`-scoped and fail on schema/catalogue identity ambiguity; trusted raw `rr:sqlQuery` is not schema-confined, and constraint-sensitive plans have no later-DDL drift/reload proof.
External SERVICE and named non-enabled source forms are rejected before query execution or connector construction.

Credential-bearing PostgreSQL/MySQL source specifications can be supplied through a bounded environment reference; parsed inline passwords fail before runtime, file or network I/O. TLS, layered configuration, telemetry and external secret-store integration remain open.
Known source-sized Rust fallback plans are rejected before backend selection or source I/O; bounded physical implementations remain planned.
SQLite has required evidence for GET/raw/form POST, ASK JSON, SELECT JSON/XML/CSV/TSV and CONSTRUCT Turtle/N-Triples/JSON-LD within the tested read-only endpoint subset.
The simple SQLite streaming-CONSTRUCT profile has a required growing-source constant-memory benchmark; this does not cover global operators.
